hemoglobin.name: Hemoglobin (Hb)
hemoglobin.description: Iron-rich protein in red blood cells responsible for transporting oxygen throughout your body.

low.explanation: Result is below the reference range. This can have multiple causes including reduced dietary iron or vitamin absorption.
low.nutritional_considerations: Consider dietary sources of bioavailable iron and vitamin C to support normal red blood cell production.
precautions: Do not start high-dose iron tablets without medical supervision.
Avoid drinking tea or coffee immediately with main meals as tannins inhibit iron absorption.

high.explanation: Result is above the reference range. This may reflect dehydration, high altitude adaptation, or other non-dietary factors.
high.nutritional_considerations: Maintain adequate daily hydration with water, buttermilk (chaas), and fresh lime water.
foods: Hydrating foods: Cucumber, Lauki (Bottle Gourd), Coconut water
precautions: Ensure proper daily fluid intake.
Discuss with your doctor if elevation persists.

hemoglobin.doctor_guidance: If Hemoglobin is below 10.0 g/dL or above 18.0 g/dL, schedule an in-person medical consultation.

rbc.name: Red Blood Cell Count (RBC)
rbc.description: Total count of circulating red blood cells carrying oxygen from lungs to body tissues.

low.explanation: RBC count is lower than the reference range, which may relate to micronutrient availability or other physiological factors.
low.nutritional_considerations: Nutrients like Iron, Folate (B9), and Vitamin B12 are critical cofactors in bone marrow erythropoiesis.
precautions: Do not self-prescribe supplements without knowing whether Iron, B12, or Folate is the primary factor.

high.explanation: RBC count is above reference range. This often reflects transient hemoconcentration due to low fluid intake.
high.nutritional_considerations: Focus on consistent hydration throughout the day.
foods: Water-rich fruits like Watermelon and Orange
precautions: Consult your physician if RBC count remains persistently elevated.

rbc.doctor_guidance: Discuss with a healthcare provider if RBC count is significantly out of range.

wbc.name: Total Leukocyte Count (WBC)
wbc.description: Immune cells defending your body against infections and foreign pathogens.

low.explanation: WBC count is below the reference range, indicating lower circulating immune cell reserves.
low.nutritional_considerations: Zinc, Vitamin C, Vitamin D, and protein support healthy immune cell maturation.
precautions: Practice good food hygiene and avoid raw unwashed street food when immune cells are low.

high.explanation: WBC count is above reference range. This is commonly a temporary reaction to minor infection, inflammation, or physical stress.
high.nutritional_considerations: Include anti-inflammatory Indian spices and wholesome antioxidant-rich meals.
precautions: If accompanied by fever, pain, or chills, seek prompt clinical evaluation.

wbc.doctor_guidance: If WBC is below 3,000 /uL or above 15,000 /uL, consult a healthcare provider.

platelets.name: Platelet Count
platelets.description: Cell fragments vital for blood clotting and wound repair.

low.explanation: Platelet count is below reference range. This can follow recent viral infections or micronutrient insufficiencies.
low.nutritional_considerations: Vitamin B12, Folate, and natural antioxidants support bone marrow thrombopoiesis.
precautions: Avoid vigorous contact sports if platelets are very low.
Seek medical attention if unexplained bruising appears.

high.explanation: Platelet count is above reference range, which may reflect reactive thrombocytosis during systemic recovery.
high.nutritional_considerations: Emphasize wholesome hydration and anti-inflammatory whole foods.
precautions: Consult your physician to rule out underlying inflammatory triggers.

platelets.doctor_guidance: If platelet count is below 100,000 /uL, clinical evaluation is advised.

hematocrit.name: Hematocrit / PCV
hematocrit.description: The percentage of whole blood volume made up of red blood cells.

low.explanation: Packed cell volume is below reference range, pointing to lower relative red cell volume.
low.nutritional_considerations: Support iron and protein intake with nutrient-dense Indian meals.
precautions: Follow up with a full Iron Profile if fatigue or breathlessness is present.

high.explanation: Hematocrit is elevated, frequently reflecting reduced plasma volume from mild dehydration.
high.nutritional_considerations: Drink adequate water and electrolyte-rich fluids throughout the day.
precautions: Rehydrate and recheck under physician guidance if it remains high.

hematocrit.doctor_guidance: Consult a doctor if PCV remains significantly out of reference range.

mcv.name: Mean Corpuscular Volume (MCV)
mcv.description: Average physical size of your red blood cells, helping differentiate between microcytic and macrocytic patterns.

low.explanation: MCV is below reference range (microcytosis, smaller red cells). In the Indian context, this is frequently seen alongside low iron stores.
low.nutritional_considerations: Focus on iron-rich staples paired with Vitamin C (Amla, Lemon) to enhance absorption.
precautions: Do not take calcium and iron at the exact same meal as they compete for absorption.

high.explanation: MCV is above reference range (macrocytosis, enlarged red cells). This pattern is commonly linked with suboptimal Vitamin B12 or Folate status.
high.nutritional_considerations: Incorporate Vitamin B12 sources (dairy, eggs, fish, or fortified foods) and folate-rich greens/legumes.
precautions: Vegetarians should discuss Vitamin B12 levels with a nutritionist or doctor.

mcv.doctor_guidance: Share MCV results with a doctor alongside Serum Ferritin and B12 values.

mch.name: Mean Corpuscular Hemoglobin (MCH)
mch.description: Average amount of hemoglobin inside a single red blood cell.

low.explanation: MCH is below reference range, suggesting pale red cells (hypochromia) typically seen in low iron status.
low.nutritional_considerations: Enhance bioavailable dietary iron intake.
precautions: Pair green vegetables with fresh lemon juice to maximize non-heme iron absorption.

high.explanation: MCH is elevated, often accompanying macrocytic patterns linked to Vitamin B12 or Folate factors.
high.nutritional_considerations: Ensure adequate daily B-complex and cobalamin sources.
precautions: Review your Vitamin B12 intake.

mch.doctor_guidance: Correlate MCH with Hemoglobin and MCV during clinical review.

mchc.name: MCHC
mchc.description: Concentration of hemoglobin in a given volume of packed red blood cells.

low.explanation: MCHC is below reference range, indicating low hemoglobin density inside red cells.
low.nutritional_considerations: Support dietary iron and micronutrient density.
precautions: Discuss with your doctor if fatigue or weakness is present.

high.explanation: MCHC is above reference range. This is rare and may relate to sample handling or specific red cell membrane factors.
high.nutritional_considerations: Maintain balanced home-cooked meals and good hydration.
foods: Wholesome Indian Thali with Dal, Roti, Sabzi, and Curd
precautions: Consult your doctor for laboratory verification.

rdw.name: Red Cell Distribution Width (RDW)
rdw.description: Variation in size and volume among circulating red blood cells (anisocytosis).

low.explanation: RDW is within or slightly below typical variation, showing uniform red blood cell sizing.
low.nutritional_considerations: Maintain balanced nutritional habits.
foods: Balanced mixed-cereal diet with seasonal vegetables
precautions: No specific dietary precautions.

high.explanation: RDW is elevated, meaning red blood cells show significant size variation. This is an early indicator of mixed nutritional factors (Iron, B12, or Folate).
high.nutritional_considerations: Comprehensive multi-micronutrient focus: combine iron, B12, and folate sources.
precautions: An elevated RDW often precedes drops in Hemoglobin; consult a healthcare professional.

rdw.doctor_guidance: High RDW warrants checking Ferritin, B12, and Folate levels.

neutrophils.name: Neutrophils Percentage
neutrophils.description: Primary white blood cells that fight bacterial infections.

low.explanation: Neutrophil percentage is below reference range, potentially after viral exposures or nutritional shortages.
low.nutritional_considerations: Zinc and Protein support white blood cell production.
precautions: Maintain good kitchen and personal hygiene.

high.explanation: Neutrophil percentage is elevated, typically representing an immune response to acute bacterial activity, inflammation, or physical stress.
high.nutritional_considerations: Emphasize anti-inflammatory, easily digestible Indian comfort foods.
precautions: If accompanied by fever, pain, or chills, seek prompt clinical evaluation.

neutrophils.doctor_guidance: Consult a healthcare provider if out of reference range.

lymphocytes.name: Lymphocytes Percentage
lymphocytes.description: White blood cells (T-cells, B-cells, NK cells) that coordinate adaptive immunity and antibody production.

low.explanation: Lymphocyte percentage is below reference range.
low.nutritional_considerations: Zinc, Vitamin D, and Vitamin A are crucial for lymphocyte function.
precautions: Discuss with your doctor if low counts persist.

high.explanation: Lymphocyte percentage is elevated, commonly following viral recovery.
high.nutritional_considerations: Continue antioxidant-rich Indian whole food nutrition.
precautions: Consult a doctor if elevation is marked or prolonged.

serum_iron.name: Serum Iron
serum_iron.description: Measure of circulating iron bound to transferrin in the bloodstream.

low.explanation: Serum iron is below the reference range, indicating reduced circulating iron available for tissues.
low.nutritional_considerations: Increase dietary intake of bioavailable iron and enhance absorption with Vitamin C.
foods: Palak / Methi Saag cooked in iron kadai
Halim / Aliv seeds in lemon water
precautions: Do not drink tea, coffee, or milk with iron-rich meals.
Do not self-prescribe high-dose iron supplements without Ferritin confirmation.

high.explanation: Serum iron is above reference range. This can occur from excessive supplementation, multiple blood transfusions, or metabolic factors.
high.nutritional_considerations: Avoid iron-fortified tonics, supplements, or heavy cast-iron cooking until medically cleared.
precautions: Stop any unprescribed iron supplements immediately.
Consult your physician for a full iron overload workup.

serum_iron.doctor_guidance: If Serum Iron is < 40 mcg/dL or > 200 mcg/dL, consult a healthcare provider.

serum_ferritin.name: Serum Ferritin
serum_ferritin.description: The primary intracellular iron storage protein; the most sensitive blood marker of total body iron reserves.

low.explanation: Serum Ferritin is below the reference range, indicating depleted iron reserves in the liver and bone marrow.
low.nutritional_considerations: Targeted iron replenishment through daily Indian superfoods and bioavailable dietary strategies.
precautions: Serum Ferritin is the gold standard for iron stores; low ferritin with normal Hb indicates latent iron deficiency.
Discuss oral iron therapy with your doctor.

high.explanation: Serum Ferritin is elevated. Ferritin is an acute-phase reactant and can rise during infection, fatty liver, or systemic inflammation, as well as true iron overload.
high.nutritional_considerations: Focus on an anti-inflammatory, low-refined-sugar, liver-supportive Indian diet.
precautions: High ferritin does not automatically mean excess dietary iron; clinical evaluation for inflammation or metabolic factors is essential.

serum_ferritin.doctor_guidance: Ferritin < 12 ng/mL indicates depleted stores; Ferritin > 300 ng/mL warrants clinical investigation.

tibc.name: Total Iron Binding Capacity (TIBC)
tibc.description: Measures the blood's capacity to bind iron with transferrin; typically rises when body iron stores are low.

low.explanation: TIBC is below reference range, which can occur during chronic inflammation or protein malnutrition.
low.nutritional_considerations: Ensure adequate daily high-quality protein and micronutrient balance.
precautions: Consult your physician to review protein status and inflammatory markers.

high.explanation: TIBC is elevated. When body iron stores fall, the liver produces more transferrin to capture available iron, driving TIBC up.
high.nutritional_considerations: Consistent iron and Vitamin C intake to replenish iron stores.
precautions: Elevated TIBC alongside low Ferritin is a hallmark pattern of iron deficiency.

tibc.doctor_guidance: Review TIBC alongside Serum Iron and Ferritin.

transferrin_sat.name: Transferrin Saturation (TSAT)
transferrin_sat.description: Percentage of transferrin iron-binding sites occupied by iron (Serum Iron / TIBC * 100).

low.explanation: Transferrin saturation is below reference range (<20%), indicating inadequate iron delivery to erythroid marrow.
low.nutritional_considerations: Prioritize iron-dense foods and avoid dietary iron blockers (tannins/phytates) during meals.
precautions: TSAT < 16% is a strong clinical signal of iron deficiency erythropoiesis.

high.explanation: Transferrin saturation is above reference range (>50%), signaling high iron availability or overload.
high.nutritional_considerations: Avoid iron-fortified cereals, supplements, and alcohol.
precautions: Consult a gastroenterologist or physician to assess iron storage status.

transferrin_sat.doctor_guidance: Consult a physician if TSAT is < 15% or > 50%.

vitamin_b12.name: Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin)
vitamin_b12.description: Vital micronutrient for nerve myelin sheath integrity, brain cognition, and red blood cell DNA synthesis.

low.explanation: Vitamin B12 is below reference range. This is extremely prevalent in India (up to 70% of adults) due to vegetarian dietary patterns.
low.nutritional_considerations: Incorporate daily dairy (curd, paneer, milk), eggs, fish, or fortified foods. Strict vegans require fortified products or supplementation.
precautions: Long-term low B12 can lead to numbness/tingling in hands and feet (peripheral neuropathy).
Discuss sublingual methylcobalamin drops or tablets with your physician.

high.explanation: Vitamin B12 is above reference range. This is most commonly caused by recent high-dose B-complex or multivitamin injections/supplements.
high.nutritional_considerations: If you are taking B12 supplements, consider pausing under medical guidance.
foods: Maintain normal balanced home-cooked Indian meals.
precautions: If you have not been taking B12 supplements, consult a doctor to evaluate liver and metabolic clearance.

vitamin_b12.doctor_guidance: If Vitamin B12 is < 150 pg/mL, clinical evaluation and targeted replenishment are strongly recommended.

folate.name: Serum Folate (Vitamin B9)
folate.description: Essential water-soluble B-vitamin needed for cellular division, amino acid metabolism, and neural tube integrity.

low.explanation: Folate is below reference range. In Indian kitchens, prolonged open boiling of vegetables often degrades natural heat-sensitive folates.
low.nutritional_considerations: Consume fresh raw sprouted salads, lightly steamed greens, and seasonal fruits.
foods: Sprouted Moong Salad with Lemon & Tomato
precautions: Do not over-boil green vegetables; steam or pressure-cook with minimal water.
Women of reproductive age should maintain optimal folate levels.

high.explanation: Folate is above reference range, typically from recent folic acid fortified foods or dietary supplements.
high.nutritional_considerations: Balanced diet with diverse seasonal produce.
precautions: Excessive folate can mask Vitamin B12 deficiency; ensure B12 is also within healthy range.

folate.doctor_guidance: Consult your doctor if Folate is < 3.0 ng/mL.

vitamin_d.name: Vitamin D (25-OH Total)
vitamin_d.description: Steroid hormone regulator of calcium-phosphorus metabolism, bone mineral density, and immune defense.

low.explanation: Vitamin D is below reference range (<30 ng/mL is insufficient, <20 ng/mL is deficient). Endemic in 70-90% of Indians due to skin melanin and indoor desk lifestyles.
low.nutritional_considerations: Expose arms and legs to 15-20 minutes of midday sunlight (11 AM - 1:30 PM). Combine with fat-containing dietary sources for absorption.
precautions: Dietary food alone rarely corrects severe deficiency (<20 ng/mL); consult your doctor regarding weekly cholecalciferol (60,000 IU) protocol.
Vitamin D is fat-soluble; take sources with food containing healthy fats.

high.explanation: Vitamin D is above reference range (>100 ng/mL), almost always resulting from excessive therapeutic supplementation.
high.nutritional_considerations: Discontinue Vitamin D supplements and maintain good hydration.
precautions: Stop high-dose Vitamin D supplementation immediately.
Check Serum Calcium to rule out hypercalcemia.

vitamin_d.doctor_guidance: Vitamin D < 20 ng/mL warrants clinical supplementation; > 100 ng/mL warrants medical review.

fasting_glucose.name: Fasting Blood Glucose
fasting_glucose.description: Measures blood glucose concentration after an overnight fast (minimum 8-10 hours).

low.explanation: Fasting glucose is below reference range (<70 mg/dL, hypoglycemia).
low.nutritional_considerations: Ensure regular meal timing with complex carbohydrates and balanced protein to stabilize blood sugar.
precautions: Do not skip breakfast.
If experiencing shakiness, sweating, or dizziness, consume a fast-acting carb and consult a doctor.

high.explanation: Fasting glucose is above reference range (100-125 mg/dL indicates impaired fasting glucose / pre-glycemic range; >=126 mg/dL warrants formal diagnostic follow-up).
high.nutritional_considerations: Focus on high-fiber whole grains (Ragi, Bajra, Oats), reduce refined white rice/sugar/maida, and include bitter greens.
foods: Methi (Fenugreek) Seeds water in the morning
precautions: A single high fasting reading does not establish diabetes; an HbA1c test and doctor consultation are necessary.
Avoid sugary beverages, sweets, and refined baked goods.

fasting_glucose.doctor_guidance: If Fasting Glucose is >= 126 mg/dL or < 60 mg/dL, consult a physician promptly.

random_glucose.name: Random Blood Glucose
random_glucose.description: Blood glucose level measured without regard to meal timing.

low.explanation: Random glucose is lower than normal baseline.
low.nutritional_considerations: Eat wholesome complex-carbohydrate meals at steady intervals.
precautions: Keep healthy snacks handy if prone to blood sugar dips.

high.explanation: Random glucose is above reference range (>140 mg/dL).
high.nutritional_considerations: Reduce simple refined sugars and portion-control carbohydrate-dense foods.
precautions: Schedule an HbA1c test and clinical evaluation with your doctor.

random_glucose.doctor_guidance: If Random Glucose is >= 200 mg/dL, seek prompt medical consultation.

hba1c.name: HbA1c (Glycated Hemoglobin)
hba1c.description: Reflects the average blood glucose concentration over the preceding 2 to 3 months.

low.explanation: HbA1c is below reference range (<4.0%), which can sometimes occur in rapid red blood cell turnover or hemolytic states.
low.nutritional_considerations: Maintain steady balanced meals.
precautions: Discuss with your physician in the context of your complete blood count.

high.explanation: HbA1c is elevated (5.7 - 6.4% reflects pre-diabetes range; >= 6.5% reflects diabetes range per clinical guidelines).
high.nutritional_considerations: Adopt a low-glycemic-index Indian meal pattern: replace refined rice/maida with Millets (Ragi, Jowar, Bajra), increase non-starchy sabzis, and incorporate legumes/paneer.
precautions: Engage in 30 minutes of daily brisk walking.
Consult an endocrinologist or physician for a comprehensive metabolic plan.
Do not start or stop medications without medical guidance.

hba1c.doctor_guidance: HbA1c >= 6.5% requires physician consultation for formal clinical evaluation.

creatinine.name: Serum Creatinine
creatinine.description: Waste product from muscle metabolism filtered entirely by healthy kidneys.

low.explanation: Serum creatinine is below reference range, often reflecting low muscle mass or lower protein intake.
low.nutritional_considerations: Ensure adequate dietary protein intake through pulses, paneer, and whole foods.
precautions: Include gentle resistance exercise to maintain lean muscle mass.

high.explanation: Serum creatinine is above reference range. This may reflect temporary dehydration, high protein/creatine intake, or reduced kidney filtration efficiency.
high.nutritional_considerations: Stay well-hydrated. Avoid excessive high-protein powders or excess sodium/salt.
foods: Steamed Rice with mild Moong Dal
precautions: Avoid NSAID painkiller medications (like ibuprofen) without doctor approval as they strain kidneys.
Consult a nephrologist or physician for a formal Kidney Function Test and eGFR review.

creatinine.doctor_guidance: Creatinine > 1.5 mg/dL warrants prompt clinical follow-up.

blood_urea.name: Blood Urea / BUN
blood_urea.description: Nitrogenous byproduct of protein breakdown excreted by the kidneys.

low.explanation: Blood urea is below reference range, which can occur with low-protein diets or high fluid turnover.
low.nutritional_considerations: Ensure balanced dietary protein distribution across meals.
precautions: No specific risk; maintain balanced nutrition.

high.explanation: Blood urea is elevated. Very commonly driven by mild dehydration, high protein intake, or reduced renal excretion.
high.nutritional_considerations: Drink adequate water throughout the day. Moderate sodium intake.
precautions: Ensure proper hydration before repeating test. Consult a doctor if creatinine is also high.

blood_urea.doctor_guidance: Consult a physician if Blood Urea is > 40 mg/dL.

egfr.name: Estimated GFR (eGFR)
egfr.description: Calculated estimate of how efficiently your kidney glomeruli filter blood per minute.

low.explanation: eGFR is below 90 mL/min/1.73m2. Values between 60-89 indicate mildly reduced filtration; <60 warrants medical attention.
low.nutritional_considerations: Focus on a kidney-friendly, moderate-salt, balanced hydration routine.
precautions: Limit processed packaged foods high in hidden sodium and phosphates.
Consult a nephrologist or general physician.

high.explanation: eGFR is within optimal filtering range (>90).
high.nutritional_considerations: Maintain current healthy kidney habits.
precautions: Continue good hydration.

egfr.doctor_guidance: If eGFR is < 60 mL/min/1.73m2, consult a physician.

sodium.name: Serum Sodium
sodium.description: Major extracellular electrolyte regulating blood volume, osmotic pressure, and nerve transmission.

low.explanation: Sodium is below reference range (<135 mEq/L, hyponatremia). Can occur from heavy sweating, fluid retention, or specific medications.
low.nutritional_considerations: Ensure balanced dietary salt and electrolyte intake, especially in hot Indian summers.
foods: Nimbu Pani with rock salt (Sendha Namak)
precautions: Avoid excessive plain water drinking without electrolytes when sweating heavily.
Consult a doctor if feeling confused or dizzy.

high.explanation: Sodium is above reference range (>145 mEq/L, hypernatremia), usually reflecting water deficit or high sodium intake.
high.nutritional_considerations: Increase plain water intake and reduce packaged salty snacks (namkeens, papads, pickles).
precautions: Reduce retail pickles (achaar) and papads high in sodium.

sodium.doctor_guidance: If Sodium is < 130 mEq/L or > 150 mEq/L, seek medical attention.

potassium.name: Serum Potassium
potassium.description: Critical intracellular electrolyte governing heart cardiac rhythm and neuromuscular contraction.

low.explanation: Potassium is below reference range (<3.5 mEq/L, hypokalemia). Can cause muscle cramps, weakness, and fatigue.
low.nutritional_considerations: Consume potassium-rich Indian fruits and vegetables.
precautions: Do not take potassium supplements without prescription.

high.explanation: Potassium is above reference range (>5.0 mEq/L, hyperkalemia). Requires medical evaluation as potassium directly influences heart rhythm.
high.nutritional_considerations: Temporarily limit high-potassium foods (coconut water, bananas, raw spinach) until doctor review.
precautions: Consult your physician promptly.
Do not consume low-sodium salt substitutes (which are often potassium chloride).

potassium.doctor_guidance: If Potassium is < 3.0 mEq/L or > 5.5 mEq/L, seek prompt medical care.

alt_sgpt.name: ALT / SGPT
alt_sgpt.description: Enzyme concentrated inside liver cells; a key indicator of hepatocellular integrity.

low.explanation: ALT is within normal baseline range.
low.nutritional_considerations: Maintain balanced liver-supportive nutrition.
foods: Fresh seasonal vegetables and home-cooked meals.
precautions: No precautions required.

high.explanation: ALT is above reference range. In the urban Indian context, mild elevations are frequently associated with non-alcoholic fatty liver (NAFLD), high refined oil/sugar intake, or medication effects.
high.nutritional_considerations: Focus on a liver-cleansing diet: minimize deep-fried foods (pakoras, puris), reduce sugar and alcohol, and emphasize sulfur-rich alliums and cruciferous vegetables.
precautions: Avoid unprescribed pain relievers or alcohol.
Consult a gastroenterologist/physician for an ultrasound and lipid workup.

ast_sgot.name: AST / SGOT
ast_sgot.description: Enzyme present in liver, heart, and muscle tissue; evaluated alongside ALT.

low.explanation: AST is within normal baseline limits.
low.nutritional_considerations: Maintain wholesome dietary habits.
precautions: No precautions required.

high.explanation: AST is above reference range. Elevated AST can reflect liver strain, intense physical exertion, or muscular stress.
high.nutritional_considerations: Incorporate antioxidant-rich foods and avoid heavy trans-fats and alcohol.
precautions: Consult your physician to review AST in conjunction with ALT.

alp.name: Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP)
alp.description: Enzyme found in the bile ducts of the liver and in growing bone tissue.

low.explanation: ALP is below reference range, occasionally seen in Zinc or Magnesium deficiency or malnutrition.
low.nutritional_considerations: Ensure adequate intake of Zinc and whole minerals.
precautions: Discuss with your nutritionist.

high.explanation: ALP is elevated, which can indicate biliary tract sluggishness, bone turnover, or active growth phases in young adults.
high.nutritional_considerations: Support biliary flow with hydration and fiber-rich greens.
precautions: Consult your physician to determine whether the source is hepatic or bone-related.

bilirubin_total.name: Total Bilirubin
bilirubin_total.description: Yellowish pigment formed during normal breakdown of red blood cells, processed by the liver.

low.explanation: Bilirubin is within normal range.
low.nutritional_considerations: Maintain wholesome dietary habits.
precautions: No precautions required.

high.explanation: Total Bilirubin is above reference range (>1.2 mg/dL). Can cause mild yellowing of sclera (eyes) and skin (jaundice).
high.nutritional_considerations: Consume very light, easily digestible, low-fat foods. Avoid fried food, heavy spices, and oils completely.
precautions: Seek medical consultation promptly.
Avoid alcohol and fatty foods.

bilirubin_total.doctor_guidance: Total Bilirubin > 2.0 mg/dL requires prompt clinical evaluation.

albumin.name: Serum Albumin
albumin.description: Major protein produced by the liver that keeps fluid inside blood vessels and transports vitamins and hormones.

low.explanation: Albumin is below reference range, suggesting lower circulating protein reserves or liver/kidney loss.
low.nutritional_considerations: Boost bioavailable dietary protein intake.
precautions: Discuss with your physician to ensure adequate protein assimilation.

high.explanation: Albumin is elevated, almost exclusively due to acute hemoconcentration / dehydration.
high.nutritional_considerations: Increase daily fluid and water intake.
precautions: Rehydrate and recheck.

total_protein.name: Total Protein
total_protein.description: Combined measurement of two major protein classes in blood: Albumin and Globulin.

low.explanation: Total protein is below reference range.
low.nutritional_considerations: Ensure every main meal includes a reliable protein component.
precautions: Review protein intake with a clinical dietitian.

high.explanation: Total protein is elevated, which can accompany dehydration or immune/globulin activation.
high.nutritional_considerations: Adequate daily hydration.
precautions: Consult your physician to review the Albumin-to-Globulin (A/G) ratio.

cholesterol_total.name: Total Cholesterol
cholesterol_total.description: Sum of all cholesterol fractions in the blood, essential for cell membranes and steroid hormone synthesis.

low.explanation: Total cholesterol is below 125 mg/dL, which can occur in malabsorption or hyperthyroidism.
low.nutritional_considerations: Include healthy monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats in cooking.
precautions: Discuss with your physician if very low.

high.explanation: Total cholesterol is above 200 mg/dL (borderline high 200-239 mg/dL; high >= 240 mg/dL).
high.nutritional_considerations: Reduce saturated and hydrogenated vanaspati fats; increase soluble dietary fiber which binds intestinal cholesterol.
precautions: Avoid deep-fried snacks (samosas, bhujia) and hydrogenated fats (dalda/vanaspati).
Engage in regular aerobic exercise.

cholesterol_total.doctor_guidance: Total Cholesterol > 240 mg/dL warrants a complete cardiovascular risk review.

ldl.name: LDL Cholesterol
ldl.description: Low-Density Lipoprotein ('bad cholesterol'); carries cholesterol particles into arterial walls.

low.explanation: LDL is well within optimal limits (<100 mg/dL).
low.nutritional_considerations: Maintain heart-healthy dietary patterns.
precautions: Optimal for arterial health.

high.explanation: LDL is elevated (>100 mg/dL optimal limit; >130 borderline; >160 high). Increases atherogenic plaque deposition risk.
high.nutritional_considerations: Adopt the soluble-fiber-rich Indian diet: Oats, Methi seeds, Psyllium husk (Isabgol), and unrefined cold-pressed oils in moderation.
precautions: Avoid commercial bakery items, trans-fats, and reuse of burned cooking oil.
Consult your physician regarding cardiovascular target goals.

hdl.name: HDL Cholesterol
hdl.description: High-Density Lipoprotein ('good cholesterol'); scavenges excess cholesterol from blood vessels back to the liver for excretion.

low.explanation: HDL is below reference range (<40 mg/dL for men, <50 mg/dL for women). Common in South Asian populations with sedentary routines.
low.nutritional_considerations: Incorporate healthy omega-3 fatty acids, exercise regularly, and replace refined carbs with healthy fats.
foods: Mustard oil / Olive oil in moderation
precautions: Aerobic exercise (brisk walking/jogging 150 mins/week) is the most potent way to elevate HDL.

high.explanation: HDL is high (>60 mg/dL), which is considered cardio-protective.
high.nutritional_considerations: Continue heart-healthy lifestyle.
foods: Maintain active lifestyle and whole food diet.
precautions: No precautions required.

hdl.doctor_guidance: HDL < 35 mg/dL warrants lifestyle and dietary intervention.

triglycerides.name: Triglycerides
triglycerides.description: The main form of stored fat in the body; surges quickly after excess carbohydrate and sugar intake.

low.explanation: Triglycerides are in the optimal healthy range (<150 mg/dL).
low.nutritional_considerations: Maintain current balanced eating habits.
precautions: Optimal baseline.

high.explanation: Triglycerides are elevated (>150 mg/dL borderline; >200 mg/dL high; >500 mg/dL very high). Highly correlated in the Indian diet with excess refined carbs (white rice, maida, sweets) and alcohol.
high.nutritional_considerations: Significantly cut down refined sugar, sweets, fruit juices, and white flour. Replace with high-fiber Millets (Jowar, Bajra, Ragi), legumes, and daily exercise.
precautions: Avoid alcohol, sweetened sodas, and Indian mithai.
Triglycerides > 500 mg/dL pose an acute pancreatitis risk; seek immediate medical consultation.

triglycerides.doctor_guidance: Triglycerides > 200 mg/dL warrants medical consultation; > 500 mg/dL requires prompt attention.

vldl.name: VLDL Cholesterol
vldl.description: Very Low-Density Lipoprotein produced by the liver to deliver triglycerides to body tissues.

low.explanation: VLDL is within normal limits.
low.nutritional_considerations: Maintain balanced nutrition.
precautions: No precautions required.

high.explanation: VLDL is elevated, paralleling high triglyceride levels.
